independentlyInspectedSourceObservations.conclusion: A retained original-to-revoker binding precedes graph effects. Preparation marks lineage and enumerates children/components with indexed durable cursors. Newly delivered descendants inherit revocation and register their own hold/cleanup. Completion permits metadata progress but stops before projection deletion. Cleanup charges deletion and exhausted probes to the same page, retires exhausted walk nodes, and only then releases component holds. Revocation ancestry and the identity journal remain retained; the recursive read/cleanup APIs are dropped.
independentlyInspectedSourceObservations.limit: The completion trigger can perform up to 100 metadata units in addition to its fixed completion bookkeeping; this is not a promise of 100 total SQL statements.

independentlyInspectedSourceObservations.conclusion: Both candidate branches retain their 101-row bound before precedence/origin checks. Native precedence and origin reads seek (context,main_version,slot) before checking principal/release identity. Correlated admission probes use the admission primary key and OFFSET 0. The large-component witness starts at the unique head admission and seeks one component member by its primary-key prefix before verifying exact principal, origin, admission and known value. Bounded probes retain missing-origin and identity validation failures rather than silently counting absent evidence.

Contribution mutations advance the component revision. Hold membership and registration increment a local pending/revision cut atomically; release advances it again. Publication materializes component/cut metadata once and the final fresh SELECT rechecks every selected generation and pending flag with recovery generation. Ordered one-row seeks check equality after LIMIT, including absent component/cut keys. The two four-statement snapshots plus one fence preserve nine SQL statements.
